subtopic: Fundamental Concepts in Organic Reaction Mechanism
stem:
Using curved-arrow notation, show the formation of reactive intermediates when the following covalent bonds undergo heterolytic cleavage.
(a) \(\text{CH}_3-\text{SCH}_3\)
(b) \(\text{CH}_3-\text{CN}\)
(c) \(\text{CH}_3-\text{Cu}\)
solution:
In each case the curved arrow starts at the bond and points to the atom that keeps the shared pair.

(a) \(\text{CH}_3-\text{SCH}_3 \rightarrow {}^{+}\text{CH}_3 + {}^{-}\text{SCH}_3\) — the bonding pair goes to sulphur, giving a methyl carbocation.

(b) \(\text{CH}_3-\text{CN} \rightarrow {}^{+}\text{CH}_3 + {}^{-}\text{CN}\) — the bonding pair goes to the cyanide carbon, giving a methyl carbocation.

(c) \(\text{CH}_3-\text{Cu} \rightarrow {}^{-}\text{CH}_3 + {}^{+}\text{Cu}\) — here the curved arrow points towards carbon, because carbon is more electronegative than copper, so a methyl carbanion is formed.

subtopic: Fundamental Concepts in Organic Reaction Mechanism
stem:
Giving justification, categorise the following molecules/ions as nucleophile or electrophile:
\(\text{HS}^{-}\), \(\text{BF}_3\), \(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{O}^{-}\), \((\text{CH}_3)_3\text{N}\!:\), \(\overset{+}{\text{Cl}}\), \(\text{CH}_3-\overset{+}{\text{C}}=\text{O}\), \(\text{H}_2\text{N}\!:^{-}\), \(\overset{+}{\text{N}}\text{O}_2\)
solution:
**Nucleophiles:** \(\text{HS}^{-}\), \(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{O}^{-}\), \((\text{CH}_3)_3\text{N}\!:\), \(\text{H}_2\text{N}\!:^{-}\). These species have an unshared pair of electrons, which can be donated and shared with an electrophile.

**Electrophiles:** \(\text{BF}_3\), \(\overset{+}{\text{Cl}}\), \(\text{CH}_3-\overset{+}{\text{C}}=\text{O}\), \(\overset{+}{\text{N}}\text{O}_2\). Their reactive sites have only six valence electrons; they can accept an electron pair from a nucleophile.

subtopic: Fundamental Concepts in Organic Reaction Mechanism
stem: Identify the electrophilic centre in the following: \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{O}\), \(\text{CH}_3\text{CN}\), \(\text{CH}_3\text{I}\).
solution: Among \(\text{CH}_3\text{H}\overset{*}{\text{C}}=\text{O}\), \(\text{H}_3\text{C}\overset{*}{\text{C}}\equiv\text{N}\) and \(\text{H}_3\overset{*}{\text{C}}-\text{I}\), the starred carbon atoms are the electrophilic centres, as they will have a partial positive charge due to the polarity of the bond.

subtopic: Fundamental Concepts in Organic Reaction Mechanism
stem:
Which bond is more polar in the following pairs of molecules:
(a) \(\text{H}_3\text{C}-\text{H}\), \(\text{H}_3\text{C}-\text{Br}\)
(b) \(\text{H}_3\text{C}-\text{NH}_2\), \(\text{H}_3\text{C}-\text{OH}\)
(c) \(\text{H}_3\text{C}-\text{OH}\), \(\text{H}_3\text{C}-\text{SH}\)
solution:
(a) \(\text{C}-\text{Br}\), since Br is more electronegative than H.

(b) \(\text{C}-\text{O}\)

(c) \(\text{C}-\text{O}\)

subtopic: Fundamental Concepts in Organic Reaction Mechanism
stem: In which \(\text{C}-\text{C}\) bond of \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Br}\) is the inductive effect expected to be the least?
solution: [Textbook error in this worked example, CORRECTED below rather than preserved, because a printed worked solution is a method a student copies. The question asks in which \(\text{C}-\text{C}\) bond the inductive effect is least; the book's printed solution answers "the bond between carbon-3 and hydrogen", which is a \(\text{C}-\text{H}\) bond — so as printed the solution does not answer its own question. The correct answer follows from the book's OWN principle, stated in the same sentence, that the effect diminishes as the number of intervening bonds increases: of the two \(\text{C}-\text{C}\) bonds this molecule has, \(\text{C}_1-\text{C}_2\) and \(\text{C}_2-\text{C}_3\), the further from the bromine on \(\text{C}_1\) is \(\text{C}_2-\text{C}_3\).] Magnitude of inductive effect diminishes as the number of intervening bonds increases. Hence, the effect is least in the \(\text{C}_2-\text{C}_3\) bond — of the two \(\text{C}-\text{C}\) bonds present, it is the one further from the bromine on \(\text{C}_1\).
_note: BOOK INCONSISTENCY, transcribed faithfully: the question asks for a C–C bond but the printed solution names "the bond between carbon-3 and hydrogen", which is a C–H bond. The molecule has only two C–C bonds (C1–C2 and C2–C3, numbering from the carbon bearing Br).

subtopic: Fundamental Concepts in Organic Reaction Mechanism
stem: Write resonance structures of \(\text{CH}_3\text{COO}^{-}\) and show the movement of electrons by curved arrows.
solution:
First, write the structure and put unshared pairs of valence electrons on appropriate atoms. Then draw the arrows one at a time moving the electrons to get the other structures.

\(\text{CH}_3-\text{C}(=\text{O})-\text{O}^{-} \leftrightarrow \text{CH}_3-\text{C}(-\text{O}^{-})=\text{O}\)

The curved arrow moves the lone pair on the singly bonded (negatively charged) oxygen into the C–O bond while the \(\pi\) pair of the C=O bond moves onto the other oxygen, so the negative charge is delocalised equally over both oxygen atoms.

subtopic: Fundamental Concepts in Organic Reaction Mechanism
stem: Write resonance structures of \(\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{CHO}\). Indicate relative stability of the contributing structures.
solution:
The three contributing structures are:

I: \(\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{C}(=\text{O})-\text{H}\)

II: \({}^{+}\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}=\text{C}(-\text{O}^{-})-\text{H}\)

III: \({}^{-}\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}=\text{C}(-\text{O}^{+})-\text{H}\)

Stability: I > II > III

[I: most stable, more number of covalent bonds, each carbon and oxygen atom has an octet and no separation of opposite charge. II: negative charge on the more electronegative atom and positive charge on the more electropositive atom. III: does not contribute, as oxygen has a positive charge and carbon has a negative charge, hence least stable.]

subtopic: Fundamental Concepts in Organic Reaction Mechanism
stem:
Explain why the following two structures, I and II, cannot be the major contributors to the real structure of \(\text{CH}_3\text{COOCH}_3\).

I: \(\text{CH}_3-\overset{+}{\text{C}}(-\text{O}^{-})-\ddot{\text{O}}-\text{CH}_3\)

II: \(\text{CH}_3-\text{C}(-\text{O}^{-})=\overset{+}{\text{O}}-\text{CH}_3\)
solution: The two structures are less important contributors as they involve charge separation. Additionally, structure I contains a carbon atom with an incomplete octet.

subtopic: Fundamental Concepts in Organic Reaction Mechanism
stem: Explain why \((\text{CH}_3)_3\overset{+}{\text{C}}\) is more stable than \(\text{CH}_3\overset{+}{\text{C}}\text{H}_2\), and \(\overset{+}{\text{C}}\text{H}_3\) is the least stable cation.
solution: Hyperconjugation interaction in \((\text{CH}_3)_3\overset{+}{\text{C}}\) is greater than in \(\text{CH}_3\overset{+}{\text{C}}\text{H}_2\), as \((\text{CH}_3)_3\overset{+}{\text{C}}\) has nine C–H bonds. In \(\overset{+}{\text{C}}\text{H}_3\), the vacant \(p\) orbital is perpendicular to the plane in which the C–H bonds lie; hence it cannot overlap with them. Thus, \(\overset{+}{\text{C}}\text{H}_3\) lacks hyperconjugative stability.
